diagnostic_evidence.quote: Here $\phi:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$ is a differentiable interaction kernel
the compactly supported interaction kernel is given by the $C^2$ Wendland function

issues.failure_explanation: With a C^1/C^2 kernel, the right-hand side of eq:MAsystem is locally Lipschitz in c. A cluster configuration is an equilibrium, and by backward uniqueness a Lipschitz ODE cannot reach an equilibrium in finite time from a non-equilibrium state. Convergence to clusters can therefore only be asymptotic. Finite-time clustering holds for discrete-time Hegselmann-Krause models, not for this continuous-time system.

failure_location.quote: the solution converges to a finite number of clusters in finite time

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restate the claim as asymptotic convergence (as t to infinity) to clusters, or as approximate clustering on [0,T].
issues.overall_effect: The modelling claim that the dynamics produce an exact quantization in finite time, motivating a finite horizon T, is unsupported.
issues.title: Finite-time convergence to exact clusters is impossible for the stated smooth dynamics
issues.why_classification: This is a local rewording of a motivational claim; no formal result or algorithm depends on finite-time convergence.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: establish the well-posedness of the problem, and derive the corresponding optimality system
Then the functional $J : H^1(\Omega) \to \R$ in Definition \ref{def:cost_functional} has a unique global minimum.
the control-to-state map $\varepsilon \mapsto c(\,\cdot\, ,T; \varepsilon)$ is not convex

issues.failure_explanation: thm:existence1 concerns the unconstrained minimization of J over all of H^1. The problem eq:OCP minimizes J over the reachable set {c(.,T;eps)}, which is nonconvex and need not contain the H^1 minimizer. Moreover, c(.,T;eps) is not shown to lie in H^1, since the nonlocal dynamics do not regularize the image I. No existence of an optimal control in the class of measurable controls is proved. The control enters nonlinearly through phi(r^eps), so convexity/Filippov-type conditions or relaxation would be needed.

failure_location.quote: The following result ensures the well-posedness of the problem

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Withdraw the well-posedness claim, stating that thm:existence1 only concerns the static functional, or prove existence of optimal (possibly relaxed) controls together with H^1 regularity of c(.,T).
issues.overall_effect: The advertised well-posedness of the Section 3 optimal control problem (and, analogously, of eq:OCP_TV) is not established; 'optimal control' eps* may not exist.
issues.title: Theorem on minimizing J over H^1 does not establish well-posedness of the control problem
issues.why_classification: Either an advertised contribution is withdrawn or a new contained existence argument is needed; the numerical method itself survives.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: However, when the control is constrained, the equality is not verified on the boundary of the compact set $E$.
we add a projection $\Pi_E$ onto the convex set $E$ to bound the control at each step

issues.failure_explanation: The sufficient-decrease test uses the full gradient norm |D|^2 even though the step is projected. At (or near) a constrained stationary point, D is nonzero on the active set and points outward, so Pi_E(eps - tau D) = eps there for all small tau. The test then requires J(eps) <= J(eps) - c tau |D|^2 with |D| > 0, which never holds. The backtracking while-loop therefore does not terminate (tau goes to 0) exactly in the constrained regime the paper anticipates.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use a projected Armijo condition, e.g. J(Pi_E(eps - tau D)) <= J(eps) - (c/tau)|eps - Pi_E(eps - tau D)|^2, or a projected-gradient norm.
issues.overall_effect: Algorithm alg:dal (and alg:admm, which calls it) is not guaranteed to terminate its line search with box constraints active.
issues.title: Projected Armijo test with full |D|^2 can fail for every step size
issues.why_classification: A standard local modification of the acceptance test restores termination without changing the method or claims.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: \STATE $\tau^{(k+1)} \gets \tau^{(k)}/b$
\STATE $\sigma^{(j+1)} \gets \tau^{(k)}$

issues.failure_explanation: In the ELSE branch, tau is enlarged while the Armijo condition holds, so the loop exits at the first tau^{(k)} that fails it. That failing step is then accepted as sigma^{(j+1)}. The update therefore need not satisfy sufficient decrease and can even increase J, contradicting the stated descent/Armijo design.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: After the expansion loop, set sigma^{(j+1)} to tau^{(k-1)} = b tau^{(k)}, the last step satisfying the condition.
issues.overall_effect: Monotone decrease of J along DAL iterations (and within ADMM's inner solver) is not guaranteed.
issues.title: Expansion branch of two-way line search returns a step violating Armijo
issues.why_classification: This is a one-line local fix restoring the intended Armijo guarantee.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: $J(\Pi_E(\varepsilon^{(j)} - \sigma^{(j)}\, D^{(j)} )) > J(\varepsilon^{(j)}) - c \,\sigma^{(j)} |D^{(j)}|^2$
which is essentially a steepest descent along the functional $J$

issues.failure_explanation: D^{(j)} is the gradient of J with respect to eps: the line search tests decrease along eps - tau D, and rmk:convergence requires D >= 0 on lower active sets. The step size is selected for the direction -D, but the update applies +sigma D. This is a gradient-ascent step for which the line-search acceptance says nothing, so J generically increases.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the update by eps^{(j+1)} = Pi_E(eps^{(j)} - sigma^{(j+1)} D^{(j)}), consistent with the line search.
issues.overall_effect: As written, alg:dal (and alg:admm through it) does not perform descent and does not deliver the claimed minimization.
issues.title: DAL control update moves along +D, an ascent direction
issues.why_classification: A single sign correction, forced by the line-search lines, restores the descent method.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: This behaviour can be encoded by an interaction kernel which quantifies the attraction between two agents
global interactions, i.e. $\phi(r_{ij}^\varepsilon)>0$ for any $i,j = 1,\ldots,N$
each agent tends to align its state $c_i$ with the states of nearby agents whose intensities are similar

issues.failure_explanation: As defined, phi(0) = -1 and phi < 0 on [0,1/4). Pairs that are spatially close with similar colour, which is exactly the set with small r_ij, therefore repel in eq:MAsystem instead of aligning. This contradicts the attraction/consensus mechanism and the requirement phi > 0 for interacting pairs. It is also not the positive C^2 Wendland function the text claims.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use the nonnegative kernel phi(r) = (4r+1)(1-r)^4 on [0,1], which is positive on [0,1).
issues.overall_effect: The specified dynamics used in the numerical tests do not produce the claimed alignment/clustering; the reported experiments are inconsistent with the stated kernel.
issues.title: Stated Wendland kernel is negative near zero, giving short-range repulsion
issues.why_classification: A local correction of the kernel formula restores consistency without affecting any other construction.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: There exists a saddle point for the functional $L : H^1(\Omega) \times L^2(\Omega;\mathbb{R}^2) \times L^2(\Omega;\mathbb{R}^2) \to \R$
$\mu \mapsto \int_\Omega \mu \cdot (v-\nabla u)$ is linear, therefore concave.
various results in the literature prove existence and uniqueness of a minimiser for \eqref{eq:cost_TV}

issues.failure_explanation: Maximizing over mu forces v = grad u, so the primal problem is inf over u in H^1 of the ROF functional K. L controls v only in L^1 (through |v|), and along v = grad u it equals K. K is not coercive on H^1: smoothed step functions have bounded TV and L^2 norm while ||grad u||_{L^2} goes to infinity. ROF minimizers generally have jumps (e.g. I the indicator of a disc yields a multiple of that indicator), lie in BV rather than H^1, and so the primal minimum is not attained and no saddle point exists in the stated spaces. In addition, the invoked minimax theorem needs a coercivity/boundedness condition in mu, which fails because L is affine in mu.

failure_location.quote: it is immediate to show coercivity in the primal variables, ensuring that the minimum is attained in a weakly compact set

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must recast the problem in different spaces (BV/measures with a suitable dual) or in the finite-dimensional discretization and prove strong duality there by a different argument.
issues.overall_effect: Existence of a saddle point and strong duality in eq:duality are unproven and false in general. The justification of the ADMM stopping criterion and of the formulation eq:OCP_TV in these spaces collapses.
issues.title: Saddle point of L in H^1 x L^2 x L^2 need not exist; coercivity claim false
issues.why_classification: The theorem as stated is false in its function-space setting. Any fix replaces the setting and proof (BV or discrete duality), so the stated result is abandoned.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: where $a = \nabla u - \frac{\mu}{\rho}$.
will converge to the unique primal solution and to one of the optimal dual ones

issues.failure_explanation: A saddle point requires (u*,v*) to minimize L(.,.,mu*), not merely that L(u*,v*,.) is constant in mu. By the paper's own shrinkage formula, the v-minimizer for a = grad u* - mu/rho differs from v* = grad u* for generic mu; for example, where grad u* = 0 and |mu| > 1 it is nonzero. Optimal multipliers must satisfy -mu* in the subdifferential of |.| at v*, so |mu*| <= 1 and mu* = -v*/|v*| where v* != 0. Hence not every mu is dual-optimal.

failure_location.quote: so that any $\mu \in L^2(\Omega; \R^2)$ becomes feasible

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the argument by the correct optimality conditions characterizing the dual-optimal set.
issues.overall_effect: The stated structure of the dual solution set is wrong, which misrepresents what the ADMM dual iterates converge to.
issues.title: False claim that every mu is dual-optimal at the primal solution
issues.why_classification: This is a local correction of an explanatory remark; no result or algorithm step depends on it.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: we lose convexity in the control-to-state map $\varepsilon \mapsto c(\,\cdot\,,T; \varepsilon)$
until the gap between the subsequent decrease and increase in the cost functional

issues.failure_explanation: Even if thm:saddle_point held, it concerns min over all u in H^1. ADMM is applied to eq:OCP_TV, where u ranges over the nonconvex reachable set {c(.,T;eps)}, with the u-step solved only locally. Strong duality over H^1 does not imply absence of a duality gap for this nonconvex constrained problem. The gap-based stopping test and the claimed primal-dual convergence are therefore unsupported.

failure_location.quote: This is the reason why Theorem \ref{thm:saddle_point} is fundamental: it ensures that there is no duality gap.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Present ADMM as a heuristic for eq:OCP_TV, dropping the no-gap justification, or prove a duality/convergence result for the controlled problem.
issues.overall_effect: The justification of alg:admm's stopping criterion and its convergence interpretation for the actual control problem is unsupported.
issues.title: No-duality-gap claim transferred to the nonconvex controlled problem
issues.why_classification: A claimed theoretical justification of the main algorithm must be withdrawn; recovering it would require a new nonconvex duality or convergence argument.
